title: Self-Healing CI/CD Evidence Contract (v2.0 payload)
description: Normalized, machine-readable, PR-provenanced evidence produced by scripts/collect_evidence.py in ci.yml and consumed by the deterministic classifier, policy engine, and remediation agent. None of those consumers parse raw tool output directly. See docs/evidence-contract.md for the full description. NOTE: the file is still named evidence-schema-v1.json for historical/path stability; its `schema_version` content field is '2.0' -- see docs/evidence-contract.md for the migration note.

scenario.description: Optional provenance only, set when evidence originated from an optional demo fixture (scripts/create_demo_failure.py / scripts/demo_submit_pr.py). Never read by the classifier, policy engine, or validator -- every decision is driven by failure_category and measurements.

event_source.description: Identifier of the collector that produced this evidence, currently always 'scripts/collect_evidence.py'.

repository.description: owner/repo of the repository the pull request belongs to.

pr_number.description: The original developer pull request this evidence was collected for.

base_sha.description: The commit the pull request is based on at collection time.

head_branch.description: The developer's branch -- the remediation fix PR targets this branch, not base_branch.

head_sha.description: The exact failing commit. The remediation agent checks out this SHA, and validate_change.py diffs the proposed fix against it, never against base_branch/main.

workflow_run_id.description: The CI workflow run id that produced this evidence, used by the remediation workflow to fetch the evidence artifact and cross-check provenance via the GitHub API.

diff_file.description: Path to a normalized, size-limited diff file (base_sha..head_sha) relative to the evidence directory.

failure_signature.description: Stable, deterministic identifier used for classification and escalation/duplicate-PR de-duplication.

concise_log_file.description: Path to a normalized, size-limited log excerpt relative to the evidence directory. Full raw logs are never handed to the agent.

relevant_files.description: The minimal set of files the remediation agent is permitted to inspect/modify, subject to policy.

measurements.description: Structured measurements for all three deterministic checks (failing test names, coverage percent/uncovered lines, benchmark medians), regardless of which one is the active failure_category, so the agent has full context.

attempt_number.description: 1 for the first and only permitted remediation attempt per failing commit. The policy engine rejects attempt_number > 1.

signature.description: sha256 hex digest over every other field (canonical, sorted-key JSON), computed by the trusted CI job that collected this evidence. Tamper-evidence for the artifact handoff across the CI -> remediation workflow trust boundary; see framework/schemas/evidence_lib.py:compute_signature and docs/architecture.md#known-limitations.
